bug_semantics: Bandit.Pipeline.determine_scheme/2 in lib/bandit/pipeline.ex copies a client-supplied request-target scheme into Plug.Conn.scheme and discards the transport secure? flag whenever the client provides any scheme. On a plaintext HTTP/1.1 listener, an unauthenticated client can send an RFC 9112 §3.2.2 absolute-form target such as GET https://victim/path HTTP/1.1; :erlang.decode_packet unwraps that as {:absoluteURI, :https, ...}, resolve_request_target!/2 stores {"https", host, port, path}, and determine_scheme returns "https". The same string arrives on h2c via the attacker-controlled :scheme pseudo-header (build_request_target!/2). Plug.Conn.Adapter.conn/5 then yields conn.scheme == :https despite no TLS. Downstream Plug.SSL can skip HTTP→HTTPS redirects, secure cookies can be emitted on plaintext, and CSRF/SameSite or audit logic that trusts conn.scheme is misled. At 1.10.4 the catch-all is still `{_, scheme} -> scheme` (pipeline.ex:84-91); 1.11.0 forces scheme from transport only.
flaw_origin: The determine_scheme catch-all that trusts a client-declared scheme was first written in PR #160 member 221dcba085289ee85adabac0bbcd9fce614c2247 (2023-06-08, Mat Trudel) to silence Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.StreamError 'request target scheme does not agree with transport' behind Envoy HTTP/2 listeners (issue #159). The member deleted the agreement-error clause (`_ -> {:error, "request target scheme does not agree with transport"}`) and added `{scheme, _} -> {:ok, scheme}` in lib/bandit/pipeline.ex:56, and rewrote HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 tests to expect the spoofed scheme instead of 400/RST_STREAM. GitHub squash-merged that identical tree onto main as ff2f829326cd5dcf7335939aef9775269d881e28. Earlier history is the opposite of this bug: 16047f9c (2022-11-25) and pipeline extraction 422651d0 (2022-12-23) required scheme/transport agreement. Later 910c8ce2 and a6aca4e2 only reshaped the already-vulnerable catch-all; they did not introduce it.

reasoning: CVE-2026-39807 / GHSA-375f-4r2h-f99j is a published CWE-807 transport-state spoof, not a withdrawn advisory. The sink is determine_scheme/2 treating a client URI scheme as authoritative. git log -L / -S on lib/bandit/pipeline.ex shows the agreement check was the pre-1.0 design (16047f9c, then 422651d0); the smallest public commit that first wrote the trusting catch-all is PR #160 member 221dcba085289ee85adabac0bbcd9fce614c2247. Immediate parent 9b71290c still errors on scheme/transport disagreement, verified on the parent blob. ff2f829326cd5dcf7335939aef9775269d881e28 is a GitHub squash aggregate of that single member (identical tree and parent, later timestamp, not an independent first-write), so it is not the BIC; 910c8ce2 and a6aca4e2 are later refactors of the same mechanism. The squash is the main-branch carrier and the CNA git-range start; first containing tags are 1.0.0-pre.6 / 1.0.0, and the fix 45feea20 lands in 1.11.0 the same day, matching the advisory range. AI attribution is judged only on the BIC commit object: Mat Trudel authored and committed 221dcba with no AI trailers or bot author. Verdict is therefore NOT_AI (real vulnerability, human authorship), not FALSE_POSITIVE.
